name.text: AROC as an expression in h (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
Let \( f(x) = {@fexpr@} \).

Find and fully expand the average rate of change of \(f\) from \(x = a\) to \(x = a + h\), then write it with the common factor \(h\) cancelled:

\( \displaystyle\dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h} = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Now let the gap \(h\) shrink to \(0\). What value does this expression approach as \( h \to 0 \)?

\( \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0}\ \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h} = \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(This limiting value is the instantaneous rate of change of \(f\) at \(x = a\) - the slope of the tangent line there.)

generalfeedback.text:
Form the difference quotient, substitute \(f\), then expand the numerator before cancelling:

\[ \begin{align*} \frac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h} &= \frac{{@fah@} - \left({@fa@}\right)}{h} \\[4pt] &= \frac{{@numExpanded@}}{h} \qquad\text{(expand }(a+h)^2 = a^2 + 2ah + h^2\text{)} \\[4pt] &= \frac{{@numCollected@}}{h} \\[4pt] &= {@ta1@}. \end{align*} \]

The middle term \(2ah\) comes from the cross term in \((a+h)^2\); dropping it is the most common slip. Every remaining term still has a factor \(h\), so the \(h\) in the denominator cancels cleanly - there is no division by zero because we cancel before letting \(h \to 0\).

As \(h \to 0\), the term(s) containing \(h\) vanish and the expression approaches

\[ \lim_{h \to 0}\ \frac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h} = {@ta2@}. \]

This is the instantaneous rate of change of \(f\) at \(x = a\): the slope of the tangent to the curve at that point. It is where the average rate of change is heading as the interval closes up, and it is the value the derivative will give.

node.description: Is the answer already free of division by h (form check)?
Correct value, and already free of /h.
(a+h)^2 = a^2 + h^2 bug: numerator collapses, answer becomes h (or kk*h).

truefeedback.text: It looks like you expanded \((a+h)^2\) as \(a^2 + h^2\) and lost the middle term. The correct expansion is \((a+h)^2 = a^2 + 2ah + h^2\) - the cross term \(2ah\) is missing from your working. Put it back, then subtract \(f(a)\) and cancel \(h\).

node.description: Restated the limit as the AROC? Or generic wrong value.

truefeedback.text: You have dropped the \(h\) term too early. Before letting \(h \to 0\), the average rate of change over the interval \([a,\, a+h]\) still depends on \(h\). Keep every term when you cancel, and leave the \(h\)-term in this first answer.

falsefeedback.text: That is not the average rate of change. Build \(\dfrac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\), expand the numerator, then cancel the factor \(h\). See the worked solution for the steps.

node.description: Still-a-quotient branch: is the value at least right (equivalent to ta1)?

truefeedback.text: This is equivalent to the average rate of change, but it is still written as a fraction over \(h\). Cancel the common factor \(h\) so no \(h\) remains in the denominator, then you will have the form the question asks for.

falsefeedback.text: Your answer still divides by \(h\), and the value is not correct either. Expand \((a+h)^2\) fully (including the \(2ah\) cross term), subtract \(f(a)\), then cancel the factor \(h\). See the worked solution.

node.description: Kept the +h term: reported the whole AROC as the limit.

truefeedback.text: Almost - but the limit is a value, not an expression in \(h\). Substitute \(h = 0\) into your average rate of change: the term with \(h\) in it vanishes, leaving the instantaneous rate.

node.description: Limit of the (a+h)^2-bug expression (h or kk*h) is 0.

truefeedback.text: A limit of \(0\) here would mean the curve is flat at \(x = a\), which is not right for this \(f\). This usually comes from losing the \(2ah\) cross term when expanding \((a+h)^2\); with the cross term kept, a non-zero term survives as \(h \to 0\). Recheck your first answer, then take the limit.

falsefeedback.text: Not the value the average rate of change approaches. Take your simplified expression in \(a\) and \(h\) and let \(h \to 0\) (set \(h = 0\)): whatever is left is the limit.

qtest.description: Both correct: simplified AROC and its limit
Unsimplified quotient for ans1 (still /h) but equivalent; limit correct
(a+h)^2 = a^2 + h^2 bug: ans1 = h (or kk*h); limit collapses to 0
Dropped h too early in ans1 (wrote the limit); kept +h in ans2
Generic wrong value for both inputs
Still-a-quotient AND wrong value for ans1
